claims.text: In FeNiCoCrMn high-entropy alloys, increased local atomic configuration heterogeneity creates barriers to dislocation motion.
Greater local atomic configuration heterogeneity increases hardness relative to a more homogeneous atomic arrangement.
Greater local atomic configuration heterogeneity increases strength relative to a more homogeneous atomic arrangement.
The degree of local ordering or disorder can be varied while FeNiCoCrMn composition is held constant in the proposed simulations.
Cluster correlation functions can quantify the proposed local atomic configuration heterogeneities.
Local bond-orientation analysis can quantify the proposed local atomic configuration heterogeneities.
Local heterogeneities disrupt uniform dislocation motion.
Heterogeneity-induced resistance to dislocation motion produces configuration strengthening.
Enhanced local misfit stresses impede dislocation nucleation.
Enhanced local misfit stresses impede dislocation glide.
Models with greater atomic-scale heterogeneity will exhibit higher yield stress under shear than the homogeneous baseline.
Models with greater atomic-scale heterogeneity will exhibit higher simulated hardness than the homogeneous baseline.
The proposed behavior is expected to apply at room temperature and within the spatial and temporal scales accessible to molecular dynamics augmented by multiscale corrections.
The hypothesis may not apply at extreme deformation rates, temperatures far from ambient, or when long-term diffusion and recovery dominate.
Molecular dynamics has limited ability to capture long-term plasticity and may exhibit scale effects.
Translation of the proposed simulation results to experimental behavior requires additional validation.
